lines.say: No food. No water. From sunrise to sunset, for a whole month! Why do millions of Muslims do this?
Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar. It starts when the new crescent moon is seen.
It lasts twenty nine or thirty days, and fasting in Ramadan is one of the Five Pillars of Islam.
Muslims believe it's the month the Quran was first revealed. Fasting helps them feel closer to God, and remember people who are hungry.
Kids, people who are sick, and travelers don't have to fast.
At sunset, families break the fast together, often with dates and water. That meal is called iftar!
And at the end of the month comes a big celebration: Eid al Fitr!
Did you know about iftar? Tell me in the comments!
